metadata.description: WCAG 2.2 database for RAG accessibility analysis supporting React, Vue, and Svelte frameworks

violations.title: Non-text Content
violations.description: All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose

code_examples.context: Missing alt attribute on informative image
code_examples.explanation: Images need descriptive alt text for screen readers

code_examples.context: Decorative image with unnecessary alt text
code_examples.explanation: Decorative images should have empty alt attributes

common_failures: Decorative images with meaningless alt text

violations.title: Name, Role, Value
violations.description: For all user interface components, the name and role can be programmatically determined

code_examples.explanation: Interactive elements need accessible names
Use semantic HTML elements for better accessibility
Use semantic elements with Vue event handlers
Use semantic elements with Svelte event handlers

violations.title: Contrast (Minimum)
violations.description: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1

code_examples.explanation: Text needs minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio with background
Interactive text must meet contrast requirements
Links must be distinguishable from surrounding text

violations.title: Labels or Instructions
violations.description: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input

code_examples.explanation: Form inputs need descriptive labels

code_examples.fix: <label htmlFor="pwd">Password</label><input type="password" id="pwd" placeholder="Enter your password" />
code_examples.explanation: Placeholders don't replace proper labels

code_examples.fix: <!-- Vue --> <label for="email">Email Address</label><input v-model="email" type="email" id="email">
code_examples.explanation: Vue inputs need proper label association

code_examples.fix: <!-- Svelte --> <label for="email">Email Address</label><input bind:value={email} type="email" id="email">
code_examples.explanation: Svelte inputs require accessible labels

common_failures: Using placeholder text instead of labels
Labels not properly associated with inputs

violations.title: Page Titled
violations.description: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose

code_examples.explanation: Page titles should describe the page content and purpose
Every page must have a meaningful title
Titles should be specific and informative

violations.title: Info and Relationships
violations.description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined

code_examples.explanation: Heading levels should follow logical sequence

code_examples.context: Using div instead of semantic heading
code_examples.explanation: Use proper heading elements for structure
Each page should have exactly one h1 element

common_failures: Multiple h1 elements on same page

violations.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
violations.description: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text together with its programmatically determined link context

code_examples.explanation: Link text should describe the destination or purpose

code_examples.context: Link without file type or size information
code_examples.explanation: Include file type and size for download links
Make link text specific and meaningful

common_failures: Links with same text pointing to different destinations

violations.title: Keyboard
violations.description: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface

code_examples.context: Interactive div element not keyboard accessible
code_examples.explanation: Use semantic interactive elements for keyboard accessibility

code_examples.context: Custom interactive element without proper keyboard handling
code_examples.explanation: Prefer native interactive elements over custom implementations
Use native button instead of custom keyboard handling
Native buttons handle keyboard interaction automatically

violations.title: Focus Visible
violations.description: Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible

code_examples.explanation: Provide visible focus indicators for keyboard users
All focusable elements need visible focus indicators
Never globally remove focus indicators

common_failures: Focus indicators that are too subtle
Missing focus indicators on custom controls

violations.title: Info and Relationships
violations.description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined

code_examples.context: Using divs instead of semantic list elements
code_examples.explanation: Use semantic HTML elements to convey structure
Use nav element and list structure for navigation
Wrap Vue router-links in semantic navigation structure

code_examples.context: Svelte navigation loop without semantic markup
code_examples.explanation: Use semantic nav and list elements with Svelte each blocks

common_failures: Using divs instead of semantic elements

violations.title: Language of Page
violations.description: The default human language of each web page can be programmatically determined

code_examples.explanation: Specify the page language for screen readers
Provide a valid language code
Use valid ISO language codes

common_failures: Missing lang attribute on html element

violations.title: Target Size (Minimum)
violations.description: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels

code_examples.context: Button too small for touch interaction
code_examples.explanation: Interactive targets should be at least 24x24 pixels

code_examples.fix: Link
code_examples.explanation: Ensure adequate touch target size
Form controls need adequate target size

violations.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
violations.description: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content

code_examples.violation: Cookie banner
code_examples.fix: Cookie banner
code_examples.explanation: Ensure focused elements remain visible when sticky content is present

code_examples.fix: <nav style="position: sticky; top: 0; height: 60px; z-index: 100;" role="navigation">Navigation</nav>
code_examples.explanation: Account for sticky/fixed content when managing focus

violations.title: Dragging Movements
violations.description: All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging

code_examples.fix: Drag me to reorder
code_examples.explanation: Provide alternative methods for drag operations

code_examples.fix: <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" aria-label="Volume"><input type="number" min="0" max="100" value="50" aria-label="Volume value">
code_examples.explanation: Provide numeric input alternative for sliders

violations.title: Redundant Entry
violations.description: Information previously entered by or provided to the user that is required to be entered again in the same process is either auto-populated or available for the user to select

code_examples.violation: <input type="email" name="email"> <!-- Later in process --> <input type="email" name="confirm_email">
code_examples.fix: <input type="email" name="email" autocomplete="email"> <!-- Later --> <input type="email" name="confirm_email" autocomplete="email">
code_examples.explanation: Use autocomplete attributes to prevent redundant entry

code_examples.violation: <select name="country"><option>Select country</option></select> <!-- Next step --> <select name="country2"><option>Select country again</option></select>
code_examples.fix: <select name="country" autocomplete="country"><option>Select country</option></select> <!-- Next step --> <select name="country2" autocomplete="country"><option value="" selected>Previously selected: [Country]</option></select>
code_examples.explanation: Provide previously entered information or auto-populate

common_failures: No mechanism to select previously entered data

violations.title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
violations.description: A cognitive function test is not required for any step in an authentication process unless that step provides at least one alternative

code_examples.explanation: Provide alternative authentication methods
Avoid cognitive function tests or provide alternatives

violations.title: Consistent Help
violations.description: If a web page contains help mechanisms, and those mechanisms are repeated on multiple web pages within a set of web pages, they occur in the same order relative to other page content

code_examples.violation: <!-- Page 1 --> <nav>Home | About | Help | Contact</nav> <!-- Page 2 --> <nav>Home | About | Contact | Help</nav>
code_examples.fix: <!-- Page 1 --> <nav>Home | About | Help | Contact</nav> <!-- Page 2 --> <nav>Home | About | Help | Contact</nav>
code_examples.explanation: Keep help mechanisms in consistent locations across pages

code_examples.context: Help contact in different page locations
code_examples.explanation: Maintain consistent placement of help information

common_failures: Help links in different navigation positions

violations.title: Status Messages
violations.description: Status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus

code_examples.explanation: Use role='status' or aria-live for status messages

code_examples.fix: Please fill in required fields
code_examples.context: Error message not announced to screen readers
code_examples.explanation: Use role='alert' for important error messages

code_examples.context: Loading state not communicated to assistive technology
code_examples.explanation: Announce loading states to screen readers
Add aria-live to Vue reactive content updates
Use aria-live with Svelte conditional rendering

common_failures: Status messages not announced to screen readers

violations.title: Bypass Blocks
violations.description: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple web pages

code_examples.fix:
Skip to main content
Long navigation menu
Main content
code_examples.explanation: Provide skip links to bypass repetitive content
Use semantic landmarks for easier navigation
Mark main content area with appropriate landmark

common_failures: Hidden skip links that don't work

violations.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
violations.description: For moving, blinking, scrolling, or auto-updating information, a mechanism is available to pause, stop, or hide it

code_examples.explanation: Provide controls for auto-playing media
Allow users to pause auto-rotating content
Avoid blinking content or provide pause controls

violations.title: Use of Color
violations.description: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element

code_examples.context: Using only color to indicate required fields
code_examples.explanation: Add visual indicators beyond color (asterisk, text, icons)

code_examples.fix:
✓ Success
✗ Error
code_examples.explanation: Use icons or text in addition to color for status

code_examples.violation: AvailableUnavailable
code_examples.context: Link state shown by color only
code_examples.explanation: Use text or styling patterns beyond color

common_failures: Required fields marked by color only
Charts or graphs with color-only legends

violations.title: Text Spacing
violations.description: No loss of content or functionality occurs by setting text spacing properties

code_examples.context: Fixed height preventing text spacing adjustments
code_examples.explanation: Allow text to reflow when spacing is increased

code_examples.context: Button not accommodating text spacing changes
code_examples.explanation: Design buttons to handle increased text spacing

code_examples.context: Navigation with fixed height cutting off text
code_examples.explanation: Use min-height instead of fixed height for text containers

common_failures: Horizontal scrolling due to fixed widths

violations.title: Orientation
violations.description: Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation

code_examples.explanation: Adapt layout instead of hiding content in different orientations

common_failures: Content only works in landscape mode

violations.title: Resize text
violations.description: Text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality

code_examples.explanation: Use relative units and min-height for scalable text

common_failures: Containers too small for scaled text

violations.title: Reflow
violations.description: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions

code_examples.explanation: Use flexible widths for responsive design

violations.title: Non-text Contrast
violations.description: Visual presentation of user interface components and graphical objects have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1

code_examples.explanation: Form controls need 3:1 contrast with surroundings

violations.title: No Keyboard Trap
violations.description: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component, then focus can be moved away using only keyboard

code_examples.explanation: Provide escape routes from focus traps

violations.title: Identify Input Purpose
violations.description: The purpose of each input field can be programmatically determined when the input field serves a purpose known to the user

code_examples.explanation: Add autocomplete attributes for common input types
Use autocomplete for personal information fields

violations.title: Motion Actuation
violations.description: Functionality that can be operated by device motion or user motion can also be operated by user interface components

code_examples.violation:
// Shake to refresh only
window.addEventListener('devicemotion', refreshOnShake);
code_examples.explanation: Provide UI alternatives for motion-based actions

violations.title: Pointer Gestures
violations.description: All functionality that uses multipoint or path-based gestures for operation can be operated with a single pointer without a path-based gesture

code_examples.violation:
// Pinch to zoom only
hammerjs.get('pinch').set({ enable: true });
code_examples.explanation: Provide simple pointer alternatives for complex gestures

violations.title: Pointer Cancellation
violations.description: For functionality that can be operated using a single pointer, completion of the function is on the up-event

code_examples.explanation: Use up-events (click) to allow cancellation

common_failures: No way to cancel accidental clicks
